reviewContext.userProblem: flying-mail has no MCP (Model Context Protocol) endpoint. Agents such as Claude Code and Codex cannot read, send or manage mail except through GraphQL, REST and the CLI, and there is no MCP surface that reuses API-key scopes, treats mail content as untrusted, and audits tool calls.
requiredOutcomes: POST /mcp on the shared hono app (Worker, Bun and Node). It is a stateless, dual-era, hand-written JSON-RPC 2.0 handler. Modern 2026-07-28 serves server/discover, tools/list and tools/call. Legacy 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18 and 2025-03-26 serve initialize, notifications/initialized, ping, tools/list and tools/call. Responses are JSON only, with no SSE and no Mcp-Session-Id (design 2).

Pipeline, in order (design 3): method, Origin, limiter configured, per-IP limit, API-key-only Bearer auth, per-key limit, Accept, Content-Type, body cap, then dispatch. Auth failure gives 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="flying-mail". Cookies are never read. /mcp is mounted before the global auth middleware. OAuth discovery paths give JSON 404s.

A new MCP_RATE_LIMITER binding (120 per 60 s, namespace_id 1002) per key and per IP. The Bun and Node servers use an in-memory limiter. The Worker answers 503 when the binding is absent. The body cap is 7 MiB.

27 snake_case tools in the fixed design 4.4 catalogue order, with annotations per design 4.2. They execute only through application use cases. tools/list hides tools whose capability the key lacks entirely (viewerHoldsCapability). tools/call re-checks, and a hidden tool is indistinguishable from an unknown one (-32602). USER_ADMIN tools are visible only to USER_ADMIN keys. No tool creates users, invites or logs in.
New use cases: resolveApiKeyViewerFromToken, trashMessages (never purges), stageAttachmentUpload and readAttachment. The REST attachment routes are refactored onto them with byte-identical responses.

Every sender-controlled string is placed only under untrusted_content, with a fixed notice in the text summary. HTML is converted to text with parse5 by default, and allowlist-sanitized HTML is returned only on request. Bodies are capped with truncation markers. Nothing is fetched.

Domain errors map to isError tool results with stable codes through the shared classifyError, and GraphQL output is unchanged. Protocol errors are JSON-RPC errors. Each tools/call produces one mcp.tool_call audit line with no content and no secrets.

README MCP server section (Claude Code, Codex config.toml, generic client, tool table, least-privilege key guidance, limits) and a flying-mail-deploy skill MCP smoke check that never prints the key. The design docs are already updated in this checkpoint.

designDecisionsAndRationale: Dual-era stateless server (design 2.2, M1). The current 2026-07-28 revision removed initialize, ping and sessions, but field clients may speak either era. Without state, nothing has to live outside Durable Objects on Workers.

Hand-written handler, no SDK (design 2.7). The SDK is not in bun.lock, and it brings zod plus Node HTTP packages. Its transport would hide the required ordering of auth, rate limits and body limits. Input validation comes from one FieldSpec per tool, which derives both the JSON Schema and the runtime parser.

API-key-only resolution (design 3.1). resolveApiKeyViewerFromToken never consults sessions and rejects tokens that do not match ^ybm_[0-9a-f]{12}_\S+$ before any hashing or lookup. The 401 is identical for missing, malformed, unknown, revoked and expired keys.
A separate MCP_RATE_LIMITER (design 3.3, M2), because AUTH_RATE_LIMITER (10 per 60 s) would throttle an agent after ten calls. The per-IP check runs before auth, and the body is read only after auth.

Visibility is a scope-presence check (viewerHoldsCapability in the single policy module). Authorization stays in the use cases. USER_ADMIN liveness is enforced at call time by requireUserAdministrator (design 4.1).

Untrusted content (design 4.5, 5): views put sender strings only under untrusted_content. HTML goes through parse5 to text, or through an allowlist sanitizer when include_html is set. No DOMPurify, because it needs a DOM that Workers lack.
Error classification is extracted into classifyError in graphql/errors.ts and shared, so MCP codes and messages equal GraphQL's (design 6).

Plan DAG: wave 1 = 01, 02, 03 and 04 (parallel, disjoint writePaths); wave 2 = 05, 06, 07, 08, 09 and 10; wave 3 = 11 (catalogue and end-to-end tests only); wave 4 = 12 (serial reconciliation and final gates). Plan 03 creates five empty tool-group stubs, and ownership of each passes to plans 05-09, serialized by dependsOn.
intentionalTradeoffs: Staged attachment ids are not bound to the uploader. This is existing behavior, accepted as a residual risk.
Clients may implement either MCP era imperfectly. This is covered by the plan 11 end-to-end tests and the plan 04 smoke check.
Hidden-text filtering in HTML-to-text is best-effort against prompt injection.
Worker CPU and memory for large base64 and HTML stay within the caps. M3 is pending user confirmation.
The Workers rate limiter fails open on binding errors, matching the accepted auth policy. It is per location and eventually consistent, so it is an abuse brake, not a quota.
A key whose creating admin lapsed still sees USER_ADMIN tools, and gets FORBIDDEN on every call.
Transport rejections (401, 403, 413, 429) are not audit events. They are bounded by the rate limits.
Wave-internal plans may see transient typecheck or test failures in each other's files. The plan 11 and plan 12 full re-runs are authoritative.
supportedEdgeCases: A session token sent as Bearer, even one matching the ybm_ format, gives 401.
A malformed Bearer token gives 401 with no hashing and no database lookup.
Absent Origin is allowed. A malformed or foreign Origin gives 403 / -32000.
A Content-Length over 7 MiB is rejected unread. A chunked body is aborted at the cap with 413.
A modern request with a mismatched MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method or Mcp-Name header gives 400 / -32020. An unsupported version gives 400 / -32022 with data.supported.

A legacy request without MCP-Protocol-Version is assumed to be 2025-03-26. A legacy initialize with an unsupported version is answered with 2025-11-25. Modern ping gives 404 / -32601. A legacy unknown method gives 200 / -32601.
Notifications give 202 with an empty body. A batch array, a JSON-RPC response object or invalid JSON give 400 with -32600 or -32700.
tools/call for a hidden or unknown tool gives -32602 and is audited as rejected, with tool "<unknown>" when the name is not a catalogue name or not a string.
A zero-scope viewer sees an empty tools/list.
move_to_trash on an already-trashed message keeps it stored, adds no new event and returns the count. A missing Trash tag gives SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE and never a hard delete.
get_attachment over 256 KiB mints a single-download, 10-minute link, which requires FILE_LINK. Staged or unreadable attachments give NOT_FOUND.
The REST attachment routes return the exact same responses, including the 404 body {"error":"Attachment not found"}.
Out-of-scope messages read as NOT_FOUND, and listings are filtered exactly as in GraphQL.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: OAuth and protected-resource metadata beyond the JSON 404s.
SSE streaming, progress notifications, MRTR input requests, the tasks extension, resources and prompts.
Binding staged uploads to their uploader.
Lower upload caps, a separate delete_messages tool, metadata-only attachment results, all-write-destructive annotations and output schemas (alternatives in M3-M7).
